items.title: Geoff Bull Interview, 1966-05-05
items.q: I knew, uh, I'll record cross because I'd listened to the George record so often and learnt the tune.

ctx.x: And that white New Orleans. Oh, well, he had bits and pieces, yeah.

I think he had the Popper Lane record, you know, the Popper Lane's children record and a few of those things. And we used to just sort of collect records. One of the first records I ever got was, and I remember when I got it I thought it was the only copy in existence in the world. I got a Bix record. And I'd read, you know, we used to read a little bit of books and that and then, and there's, you know, all these glorious mysteries that shroud characters like Bix because he was a big hard drinker and died young…
You mean, were they playing like Dix or Latin Air?
Who are your favourites, by the way?

Favourite musicians are Manuel Paul, for one, I don't know what you're just talking about. Captain Handy. George. Lewis. Jim. I like Lewis Nelson very much. I like Jim better. Dee Dee knocked me right out the night I heard Dee Dee. I've only heard him once, but that was tremendous. And Billy, of course, was good. She didn't play on the night, but she sang. And they did a couple of duets, which were really tremendous. I like Kid Thomas. I like Chester's artist very much. And Dre, I've only heard a couple of times,…
